claims.sentence: Participants completed several measures including the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) and daily sleep diaries at pre-treatment, post-treatment, and at 1, 2, and 3 months after treatment.</jats:p> </jats:sec> <jats:sec> <jats:title>Results</jats:title> <jats:p>From pre-treatment to 3-month follow-up, significant and large decreases in insomnia severity were observed in both ISR (M = -5.91 units, p < .001, d = -1.99) and TSD (-5.41 units, p < .001, d = -1.82).

claims.sentence: From the same pre-treatment to 3-month follow-up period, a significant and moderate reduction in sleep onset latency was observed for the ISR group (M = -11.66 min, p < .05, d = -0.76), but not for the other two groups.</jats:p> </jats:sec> <jats:sec> <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title> <jats:p>Both ISR and TSD were effective in reducing insomnia symptoms severity, but ISR produced a superior treatment response on sleep onset latency and this improvement was generally maintained up to 3 months after treatment.</jats:p> </jats:sec> <jats:sec> <jats:title>Support (if any)</jats:title> <jats:p>This research was supported by a grant from the Canadian Institutes of Health Research (#148410).</jats:p> </jats:sec>
